oixcloud-login: Use an Access Token, email and password, or Google for an existing account.
The example email is fictional; no password is shown.
After sign-in, wait for nodes to load before connecting on Home.
oixcloud-connect: Start the VPN after loading nodes. Allow the first VPN configuration request.
Select a node. If a network profile fixes the outbound, change that profile first.
Connection state, mode and Final Route are separate. Verify the actual exit.
oixcloud-proxies: Select a node or Best Available
Search the list for the node you need.
Select an automatic entry or group
These entries select an outbound; they do not open another editor.
Select a node and choose Done
Verify a new connection. The latency values are examples only.
oixcloud-filter: Choose Any, Only or Exclude for lines and regions. Available tags depend on the account.
Names accept regular expressions. Preview search does not change the filter.
Only some lines are shown here. Wait for managed nodes to refresh after saving.
oixcloud-policies: Choose Manual, URL Test, Fallback, Load Balance or Smart for your needs.
Add members and check the relay
The example has two nodes. Leave Underlying Proxy as None if not needed.
More Health Check options are below. Select the saved group on Home or in a rule.
oixcloud-chains: Build a proxy chain in order
Use a name that describes its purpose.
Eligible policy groups can be the first hop only. Test nodes individually first.
Check Route Preview. Select the saved chain on Home or in a rule.
oixcloud-rules: Add a routing rule for a website
Enter example.com without a scheme or path.
The example uses an existing group named Work.
Use Rule mode and make a new request to verify the matched rule.
oixcloud-dns: The example matches the suffix of an internal domain.
Send only matching domain queries to the selected resolver.
192.0.2.53 is a documentation address. Replace it with your reachable DNS server.
oixcloud-networks: Match the exact Wi-Fi SSID. Configure cellular networks separately.
Direct mode differs from sending only unmatched traffic direct.
Empty DNS inherits global settings. Rules and IPv6 can inherit independently.
oixcloud-mitm: This example has a generated certificate but no signed-in account.
Complete installation and full trust in iOS Settings.
Account actions are unavailable while signed out. Do not replace local certificates casually.
oixcloud-modules: Add Module, Import Module, Subscribe Module and Kelee Module Hub are separate actions.
Names and content are fictional. Enable what you need; long-press for actions.
Adjust runtime priority here when modules affect the same domain.
oixcloud-sync: Enable sync on the main Settings page first. Use Sync Now here.
MITM syncs rule sets. This switch does not sync device certificates.
Use the same Apple Account on both devices and enable sync on TV too.
oixcloud-tailscale: Add and authorize a Tailscale network
The names identify this network and this device.
Use Save and Log In, then authorize this device in the browser.
Automatic Routing handles peers and approved subnets. Choose internet exit routing separately.
oixcloud-automation: Check the source and client API
Select the API expected by the script. Its name becomes the page title.
Test manually first, then enable schedules or network events.
JavaScript and Run Now are below the triggers. Scroll down to continue.
oixcloud-requests: Inspect the route used and the reason for the decision.
After changes, make a new connection and verify the rule and outbound.
oixcloud-mitm-generate: Generate Certificate appears when no local certificate exists.
Installation and trust actions appear after generation.
Install the local profile and enable full trust in iOS Settings.
flclash-login: Google, Access Token and email/password sign-in are supported.
This confirms the form. No real account or token is shown.
Return to the account page and wait for the managed profile to finish syncing.
flclash-connect: On desktop, enable System proxy or TUN as needed.
Select nodes in the relevant group on Proxies.
Use the Status card’s play button
The start control is inside this card, not fixed at the bottom-right corner.
flclash-proxies: Select a node in its group
Each group has its own choice. Change the group that handles your traffic.
The theme color marks the selected node.
Latency is a test result, not proof that every app or website works.
flclash-profiles: This is an ordinary URL profile. Managed profiles sync from the account page.
Edit, Override, Sync, Proxy chains, More and Delete are separate actions.
More includes runtime-profile actions. Managed profiles do not offer identical exports.
flclash-filter: Cycle Any, Only and Exclude. Available tags depend on the account.
The right-hand preview follows your conditions. Search only locates entries.
Restore default is at the top. Wait for account refresh and profile sync.
flclash-chains: Profile menu → Proxy chains → Add or edit
Available nodes and supported groups appear below the chain.
Reorder the hops here. Per-hop latency is not full-chain latency.
For a node exit, select its derived (via …) entry. The original node keeps its route.
flclash-override: Order: Standard, Overlay, Custom, Script. Overlay is selected here.
Keep personal rules and groups on top of the subscription.
Use the title-bar check and Apply now to validate and apply changes.
flclash-rules: Override → Edit custom routing → Rules → Add
Form and Rule text are separate editing modes.
Basic info contains the type, content and an existing rule target.
A preview is below. Check and apply, then verify a new request.
flclash-capture: System proxy and Bypass domains affect apps that follow system proxy settings.
After enabling it, verify authorization, routes and actual traffic.
This option is macOS-only. Windows has a different set of options.
flclash-dns: Add fields with the top + button
Unadded fields inherit the profile. Remove an entry using its left-hand control.
Change one field at a time
Values are examples only. Quick edit is also available at the top right.
A custom profile’s own settings take precedence. Restore original values if needed.
flclash-backup: Keep the current state before major changes or restoring another backup.
Compatible updates matching records. Override removes content absent from the backup.
After choosing Restore, select configuration files only or all data.
flclash-restore: Restore profiles, scripts and rules while keeping app settings.
Also apply the backup’s application and network settings.
Scope and Compatible/Override strategy are independent choices.
flclash-webdav: Enter your own WebDAV address, preferably HTTPS.
Portable backups omit this password. Enter it again on a new device.
Make a manual backup and confirm a new remote entry afterwards.
flclash-tailscale: The current login method is a segmented control, not a dropdown.
Scroll to Save and log in
Continue below Automatic routing, Exit node and Advanced to authorize.
flclash-android: Choose which apps enter the VPN
Turn on from the More menu
The top-right menu enables or disables app access control.
More → Settings → Mode. Whitelist mode includes only selected apps.
Use the top-right checkmark. The bottom bar shows the mode and selected count.
flclash-diagnostics: Run the check from the title bar
The adjacent control copies the diagnostic report.
Distinguish profile, core, local entry, capture and DNS checks.
More DNS/HTTPS checks are below. A pass does not validate every app or node.
helper-surge: Wait for account and node retrieval before opening Connection.
Select nodes in Surge for mapping mode, or in Helper for single-port mode.
Use Apply in Surge and confirm Surge selected the generated profile.
helper-lan: Configuration delivery and proxy traffic use different ports.
Use dedicated LAN credentials, not the oixCloud account password.
Other devices use this Mac’s LAN IP. Update their settings after changes.
oixclash-login: Use an Access Token, or choose email and password.
Copy the token from the website or app. It is not a subscription URL.
Check the plan, enable the plugin, then save and apply at the page bottom.
oixclash-running: Wait for Running status, then verify a LAN connection.
Uncommon ports go direct by default. Adjust only as needed and retest.
Device policies, DNS and custom rules follow. Save and apply at the bottom.
oixclash-rules: Read and save shared account rules
Reading replaces unsaved edits. Keep anything you need before reloading.
Use DIRECT, REJECT or a group already present in the configuration.
Saving affects other clients using these account rules. Verify a new connection.
